avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce letrozole levels and efficacy in hormone-sensitive breast cancer
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consult oncologist before use

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild estrogenic activity; theoretical concern in hormone-sensitive conditions
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for reduced letrozole efficacy; discuss with healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Red Clover
caution_supplements.mechanism: Contains isoflavones with potential estrogenic effects that may counteract letrozole
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution and medical supervision in breast cancer patients

caution_supplements.name: Calcium Supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May slightly reduce letrozole absorption if taken simultaneously

caution_foods.name: Soy products (high intake)
caution_foods.mechanism: Isoflavones possess weak estrogenic activity; excessive intake may theoretically reduce aromatase inhibitor efficacy
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption; avoid excessive soy supplementation in hormone-sensitive breast cancer

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase letrozole levels; limited clinical significance with letrozole
caution_foods.action: Moderate intake; monitor for adverse effects if consuming large quantities

monitoring_notes: Letrozole is minimally metabolized and has few major interactions, but vigilance regarding estrogenic supplements is warranted in breast cancer patients. Monitor for reduced efficacy (hot flashes, joint pain control) or signs of estrogen rebound if estrogenic substances are co-administered.
